reply_text:
㊢ (the note) The findings are in `/tmp/pyreg/overnight/TN-lean-continued-port-review.md`, alongside the other curriculum notes. Since `/tmp` doesn't survive a reboot, I can copy it into the repo's docs if you want to keep it. Shall I go ahead with the proposals at the end of the note: probe `.loop` at `f5d4594` and re-pin there, then bell the transpiler changes to codex-18 and codex-19?

㊢ (what it covers)
- **codex-17:** keep all of the integration work, which is at 20 of the 110. Two flaws: the merge `f5d4594` went in without a probe of its own, and the test commit `00e5c04` dropped an assertion.
- **Lisp port:** codex-18's hand port and codex-19's transpiler share one branch, and neither has compiled any of the 110.
- **Threading:** the Python port never starts a thread on the startup path. The transpiler builds threading only because it translates every import.
- **Proposals:** five, listed at the end of the note.

㊟ (how the review was done) I've marked in the note which claims I checked myself: the Array.extract fix diff, the merge reflog, that the merged tree is identical to the probed commit, the threading call sites, and the uncommitted Python edit. The rest comes from the three readers, with transcript line numbers. I reran no tests.
